metadata.description: One firmware build as a fact about the estate, named by its maker, the device model it is for and its version. A Knowledge class: discovered, never provider-realized. A device that states this maker, model and version runs this build: the match is derived and no edge is stored. A SoftwareBillOfMaterials describes the build and lists what is in it.

manufacturer.description: Who makes the device the build is for, written as the device states it (Redfish Manufacturer).

model.description: The device model the build is for, written as the device states it.

version.description: The version, written as a device that runs the build reports it.

adopts.role: firmware as a thing of its own beside the devices it runs on — the Manufacturer and Version vocabulary this class's fields align to

context.purpose: Records a firmware build as a fact — the thing a device runs, and the subject its software bill of materials describes — so one advisory about a build reaches every device that runs it.
context.plain_description: One firmware build, identified by who makes it, the device model it is for and its version, each written exactly as a device reports it. It is knowledge about the estate, never provisioned. Nothing ties it to a device by a stored edge: a device already states its maker, its model and the firmware version it runs, and a device that states the same three values runs this build. So twenty switches on one build share one record, and a device that is updated stops matching the old build without anyone editing either record. What is inside the build is not listed here: a SoftwareBillOfMaterials describes it and lists its components, one today for most devices and many where a maker publishes a full list.
use_when: You need every device tied to the exact firmware build it runs, deduplicated across the fleet.
You need the subject a firmware bill of materials hangs from: build ← document → packages → vulnerabilities.
not_for: The device — NetworkSwitch, NetworkGateway, WirelessAccessPoint and the other device classes state the version they run; this is the build as a fact.
A container or operating-system image — SoftwareImage, identified by its digest.
A component inside the build — SoftwarePackage, listed by the build's SoftwareBillOfMaterials.
A host's boot firmware settings — the Machine `firmware` element.
works_with: NetworkSwitch, NetworkGateway and WirelessAccessPoint — the devices that run a build, matched by the maker, model and firmware version each one states.
SoftwareBillOfMaterials — the document that describes the build and lists its components.
